harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: WebDAV is operational at http://node1:8080/documents/. The supplied editor account has authenticated CRUD access; anonymous requests receive 401; exclusive locks reject tokenless overwrites with 423 and accept token-authorized updates. Original project files remain unchanged. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 were retained, and all functionality recovered after a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Created a separate writable workspace under /var/lib/webdav while preserving /srv/legacy2/webdav-document-locks.
Configured editor-only WebDAV, persistent locking, SELinux labels, TCP/8080, firewalld, and automatic service startup.
Verified authenticated create, read, replace, delete, LOCK, tokenless overwrite denial, token-authorized overwrite, and UNLOCK.
Restarted node1 safely and repeated service, data, CRUD, authentication, and locking checks.
Removed test artifacts and restricted the lock database files to mode 0600.

evidence.requirement: WebDAV workspace at /documents/ on TCP port 8080 with supplied documents
evidence.summary: Configuration validation, listener output, authenticated PROPFIND, successful document reads, and byte-for-byte content comparisons prove the endpoint.

evidence.requirement: Editor can create, read, replace, and delete documents
evidence.summary: Direct pre- and post-restart workflows returned the expected 201/200/204/404 statuses with content comparisons passing.

evidence.requirement: Exclusive locks prevent overwrite without the lock token
evidence.summary: LOCK succeeded, tokenless PUT returned 423 with unchanged content, token-bearing PUT returned 204, and UNLOCK succeeded.

evidence.requirement: Anonymous clients cannot access the workspace
evidence.summary: Repeated anonymous GET requests returned 401 while the supplied editor credentials authenticated successfully.
Initial and final SHA-256 hashes for access.txt, brief.txt, and budget.csv are identical; live copies also match the protected originals.

evidence.requirement: Retain the installed OS release and kernel and use compatible software
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remained installed; httpd 2.4.63 came from signed enabled RHEL repositories.

evidence.requirement: Security controls and clean final state
evidence.summary: SELinux remains enforcing with no current-boot AVCs, firewalld exposes TCP/8080 persistently, credentials are restricted, no failed units or test residue remain, and lock files are mode 0600.
Evidence captures the healthy baseline and old boot ID, acknowledged native reboot, changed boot ID, restored services/firewall/data, and successful post-restart CRUD and lock behavior.
